chapter: Working life: spot jobs, day jobs, nightclubs
title: Spot work, fraternity dances and Sunday picnics
summary: He preferred spot jobs, worked nightly with Brownlee and Hardy on fraternity dances, and played Sunday picnics for good money.

bands.name: Norman Brownlee and Emmett Hardy's band

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: what kind of jobs did you work in those days uh you'd have pretty steady jobs for a while and then spot

well i worked mostly spot work see i took mostly spot jobs i didn't care nothing about study work i didn't want too much work anyhow you know because i was working in the daytime and i didn't care about too much work but uh when i worked with norman brownlee and and uh and emmon hardy we used to work every night in the week spots every night we had a spot we worked from the lower coast in algiers all the way up to harvey and and and all the way from the barracks to calton avenue in the city and we got most of the fraternity work on this side of the river we had practically every night sold up with fraternity dances that must have kept you awful busy yeah it was busy it's too busy
no music during the day during those times
did anybody watch during the day no very little music during the daytime very little most of it was at night did you play any picnics yes play picnics at millenburg west end bucktown
what day would they be sunday's mostly well that didn't interfere with your job at all no no
uh-uh no that was mostly on the sunday go out there catch the train at 8 30 and get out there for nine o'clock go to work at nine play till six for two and a half all day that was a little money
